Package org.aeonbits.owner.loaders

Class EnvDialect

java.lang.Object
org.aeonbits.owner.loaders.EnvDialect
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable
public final class EnvDialect extends Object implements Serializable
The rules by which a DotEnvLoader reads a .env file.

There is no standard for .env: every tool that reads one has invented its own rules, and they disagree on the points that matter most — whether quotes delimit a value or belong to it above all. A dialect is therefore not a format but a name for a bundle of answers, and this class is that bundle. The named constants are the common combinations; any of them can be adjusted one answer at a time with the with… methods, so a tool not named here can still be described.

The default is DOCKER, which does nothing at all to a value: whatever follows the = is the value. It is the behaviour of docker run --env-file, it is close to what SmallRye Config does in the Java ecosystem, and on a format with no standard the defensible default is the one that transforms nothing. When it is the wrong guess it is wrong visibly — a value arrives with its quotes still attached, which is noticed at once — where stripping quotes that were meant to be kept removes characters and says nothing.

No dialect interpolates ${…}. OWNER expands variables in property values itself, after loading and across every source, so a loader doing its own would expand them twice.

2.0.0

    • DOCKER

      public static final EnvDialect DOCKER
      The rules of docker run --env-file, and the default: quotes are part of the value, nothing is unescaped, # starts a comment only at the beginning of a line, and a bare name takes its value from the environment.

    • DOTENV

      public static final EnvDialect DOTENV
      The rules of the dotenv family — the Node, Python, Ruby and Go packages, and dotenv-java: quotes delimit, escape sequences are expanded inside double quotes, a leading export is dropped, a # preceded by whitespace starts a comment, and a quoted value may span lines.

    • COMPOSE

      public static final EnvDialect COMPOSE
      The rules of env_file in Docker Compose, which — unlike docker run --env-file, and this is the trap — does treat quotes as delimiters. It recognises no export prefix and does not accept a value spanning lines.
